transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-05
Time: 14:30 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Daniel Park (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Alex Gomez (Redwood CSM), Sofia Martinez (Helix Eng Lead), Liu Wei (Helix Platform), Amir Khan (Helix Security), Nora Patel (Helix Product), Ravi Desai (Helix Infra)
---
[00:00] Daniel Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll wait another 30 seconds for the last folks, um, but go ahead and, uh, start with a quick run through of status, so today's goal is staging access + quick read on the micro-benchmarks and blockers.
[00:18] Sofia Martinez: yep, good — thanks Daniel. we got the invite, looks like all the infra bits are there but we hit two things when we tried the gateway: the IP allowlist isn't final and the token rotation docs were a little unclear.
[00:32] Daniel Park: ok noted. Priya, can you walk through the staging topology we spun up? I know we created a small dedicated pool for the pilot to test tail latency.
[00:41] Priya Nair: sure — so in staging we provisioned a 2-gpu pool, 1xA100-ish instance for steady load and a burst lane, uh, we set up prefix caching/KV cache with default hit-rate target of 60% to start. routing policy is regional to us-east-1, and we applied a minimal qps throttle to avoid cold-start storms. there may be some noisy neighbors on the instance we used, so that explains a bit of the variance.
[01:05] Liu Wei: quick question — is that the KV "cash" or cache — I saw K-V cash in the logs, the stt provider misread it.
[01:10] Priya Nair: yeah, it's kv cache, just spelled weird in some auto-logs. the important part is hit-rate and the prefix keys, we can tune TTL and shard count.
[01:19] Ravi Desai: the allowlist is the thing blocking us, our infra team can't curl the gateway from staging until we get the IP ranges. we asked for the CIDR yesterday but didn't get the final list.
[01:29] Daniel Park: apologies, that's on us — we'll circulate the IP set after the call, and include the ephemeral ranges for burst pools. Alex, can you confirm who will send that?
[01:37] Alex Gomez: I'll send the allowlist + step-by-step token rotation guide in an email and attach the doc link: redwood.internal/poc/helix-access.md (note: placeholder link) — expect that within 24 hours.
[01:48] Nora Patel: on the bench results, we ran the micro-benchmark that Nora's team put together — sorry, that was Ravi — we saw average latency fine but p95 and p99 jumped under concurrent spikes.
[02:02] Priya Nair: that's consistent with what we expected given the initial KV hit-rate and the chosen batching window. two levers: increase batch size slightly to amortize kernel overhead, and raise kv cache TTL so more prefixes hit. there's a tradeoff on latency tail vs cost.
[02:18] Sofia Martinez: how much cost are we talking about if we increase batch size? our finance team is watching token spend; they want to cap model spend.
[02:27] Daniel Park: good point — we can run controlled runs and provide an estimated delta. Priya, can you do a quick cost vs p99 table?
[02:35] Priya Nair: yes, I'll produce a small matrix. rough ballpark: moving from batch size 8 to 16 reduces compute per-token by ~12% under steady load but may add 10-20ms to cold tail cases; with the KV hit-rate improvement it's usually net positive for throughput. I'll include quantized model tradeoffs too.
[02:53] Amir Khan: security question — KMS integration: are keys customer-managed? we need to know where the keys live, HSM or managed KMS, and audit log retention. also SOC2 evidence.
[03:05] Daniel Park: we support customer-managed keys via KMS integration; you can bring your own in the Private deployment and for Dedicated; hosted has Redwood-managed KMS by default but we can discuss options. we have SOC2 docs, I'll share the artifacts and the SOC2 report redacted copy.
[03:20] Amir Khan: great. also need to see audit logs with user identity and token rotation events.
[03:25] Priya Nair: we capture request-level traces and token events in the audit stream; retention depends on plan, but for the pilot we can keep higher retention and forward logs to your SIEM via secure syslog or cloud logging.
[03:38] Sofia Martinez: back to the benchmarks — we ran three profiles: interactive chat (short-turn), summarization (long context), and bulk embeddings. embeddings looked fine, summarization had more variance.
[03:51] Priya Nair: summarization often stresses KV caching more because of longer KV keys, and also the runtime kernel selection can change with sequence length. if you can share a failing trace we can correlate with the kernel switch.
[04:04] Sofia Martinez: I'll upload traces to the shared sheet. current sheet: google.com/sheet/helix-poc-bench (placeholder).
[04:10] Daniel Park: great, please put a label on any p99 spikes. Priya will pick two worst traces.
[04:16] [04:16] Priya Nair: okay, will do. also, one config note — we defaulted to a quant profile that's safe for quality; if you want to push more aggressive quantization (int4 or mixed) we can test but need evals.
[04:29] Nora Patel: product question — if we hit latency SLOs in staging, what's the path to prod? how long to scale?
[04:36] Daniel Park: for Dedicated we have capacity-commit timelines — generally 2–4 weeks to provision dedicated pool depending on region; if you want private on-prem that's a longer integration. for most customers, we move to a reserved pool and ramp concurrency with canary.
[04:50] Liu Wei: for now we want to validate the canary approach. also — side note — any network egress costs we should model?
[04:57] Daniel Park: yes, we'll give a cost primer including egress and token compute. Priya will attach a cost worksheet with the batch profiles.
[05:05] Amir Khan: coming back to keys — if we use customer-managed KMS in Dedicated, do we need to pre-provision IAM roles?
[05:12] Priya Nair: yes, we'll need a service account with KMS decrypt access; we'll template the IAM policy. that's in the security doc we'll share.
[05:20] Sofia Martinez: one blocker: our staging test harness expects an API key per-test-run; is there a recommended rotation cadence? we don't want long-lived keys in CI.
[05:30] Daniel Park: rotate tokens daily is common for CI; we can issue short-lived tokens via the gateway or bring your own token broker — we'll document both approaches. Alex will include the token rotation guide.
[05:41] Ravi Desai: when you say short-lived, do you mean OAuth-style tokens or API keys? we prefer OAuth-like ephemeral tokens to avoid secrets leaking.
[05:49] Priya Nair: we support both. for ephemeral tokens we do a signed token flow that expires in minutes and leverages your identity provider; we can show a demo.
[05:58] [06:00] Daniel Park: ok let's pivot: quick read on the micro-bench numbers you shared this morning. Sofia, you said p95 was 320ms and p99 850ms under bursts, is that right?
[06:09] Sofia Martinez: yes, for the chat short-turn profile under a 200 qps spike, averages were ~60–80ms, p95 320, p99 around 850. under steady 40 qps, p99 dropped to ~180.
[06:21] Priya Nair: that suggests the backend can handle steady concurrency but the burst is causing tail queuing — we can enable a slightly larger prefetch window and increase concurrency on the burst lane; also bump kv cache TTL to improve hit-rate during spikes.
[06:34] Liu Wei: how will that affect cold starts? we saw a few cold start bumps in the first 10 minutes.
[06:40] Priya Nair: cold starts are influenced by kernel cache warming; we have a warmup probe option that keeps a thin replica warm, small CP cost but reduces cold tail significantly.
[06:49] Amir Khan: any additional attack surface with warmup probes hitting the endpoint? we need logs and auth consistent.
[06:55] Priya Nair: warmup probes authenticate with ephemeral tokens and are logged like any other request; we'll include that in the audit stream.
[07:03] Daniel Park: I'm going to propose outcomes and owners — Alex will send access docs; Priya will run two tuning passes (batch size & kv TTL) and re-run benchmarks; Amir, you'll check KMS questions; Liu will confirm VPC peering; Sofia/Ravi will upload failing traces. does that sound right?
[07:22] Sofia Martinez: yep, that works. timeline ok? we need results before our sprint end on Friday.
[07:28] Daniel Park: timeline: we'll aim to have a tuned benchmark run and a results sheet by Friday 2026-10-09.
[07:35] [07:35] Priya Nair: noted — I'll capture the config diffs in the sheet, include the exact batch sizes and TTLs. expect two runs: conservative and aggressive.
[07:44] Nora Patel: one more product ask — we want to see a cost projection for the two configs so PM can sign off.
[07:50] Priya Nair: will add cost delta per 1M tokens and per-hour for the burst lane.
[07:56] Daniel Park: ok, anything else on the infrared? (laugh) infra?
[08:01] Ravi Desai: small ask: can you include egress IPs for burst pools separately? we need to whitelist them.
[08:07] Alex Gomez: yes, will include separate allowlist for burst pools.
[08:11] Amir Khan: and please include sample audit log entries so we can map fields to our SIEM.
[08:16] Daniel Park: will do. final wrap: we'll send follow-ups — Alex will email allowlist + token guide within 24 hours; Priya will post tuning matrix and run second benchmark by Friday; Amir will send security Q's by Thursday; Liu will confirm networking by Wednesday.
[08:31] Sofia Martinez: great, thanks everyone.
[08:33] Daniel Park: thanks — we'll reconvene same time next week unless we need a mid-week deep-dive. Priya — can you propose 1 hour slot for deep-dive around quantization?
[08:42] Priya Nair: yes, I'll propose Wed 10/12-11am ET.
[08:47] Daniel Park: perfect. thanks all.
[08:50] [End of recording]
